description: What the main window may do. `core:default` is Tauri's own baseline and is kept as it stands: the main window already held it before this application declared an ACL manifest, so narrowing it would change what works today and belongs to its own change, not to this one. Note that `core:default` IS a set of plugin permissions - the resolver turns every `core:<name>` key into `plugin:<name>|<command>` - so this window holds Tauri's own window, event, webview, path, app, image, resources, menu and tray commands. What is granted here is no THIRD-PARTY plugin: no filesystem, no shell, no HTTP, not the clipboard plugin, and each would have to be added deliberately. The network is closed by the CSP's `connect-src` in tauri.conf.json, not by this file. `allow-describe-displays`, `allow-describe-shortcuts` and `allow-describe-shortcut-status` are the reading commands of this crate the main window calls - the monitor list, the static shortcut registry, and what the operating system answered when that registry's capture combination was offered to it at startup; none of the three captures a pixel. `allow-capture-region` is the one that does: ADDED ON 6 SEPTEMBER 2026, it runs the very `veil::perform_capture` the global shortcut runs, so that the launcher's headline tile stops being a button that looks pressable and reaches nothing. It is the widest grant in this file - the primary screen into memory, and a full-screen always-on-top sheet over the desktop - and it is deliberately absent from `capabilities/veil.json`: the veil is what a capture PUTS on screen, and starting one from inside it would freeze a screen that is already frozen. The five `veil_*` commands are deliberately absent, so the ACL refuses them here as well as `ipc::ensure_from` does. `local` is stated rather than left to its default, and no `remote` block exists: that absence is what makes `!is_local` refuse any non-local origin outright. THE FOUR `core:window:*` LINES ADDED IN THE NIGHT OF 5-6 SEPTEMBER 2026 pay for the custom title bar, which exists because `decorations` is now `false`: `allow-minimize`, `allow-toggle-maximize` and `allow-close` are the three controls the bar draws, and `allow-start-dragging` is what moves the window when the bar is pressed - that last one is invoked by Tauri's own drag-region script rather than by our code (tauri-2.11.5/src/window/scripts/drag.js:103-104), which is exactly why it is the easy one to forget. Each is granted BY NAME because `core:window:default` does not hold it; that set was read in this build's own gen/schemas/desktop-schema.json, and it does already hold `allow-is-maximized` (which of the two glyphs to draw) and `allow-internal-toggle-maximize` (double-click the bar), so neither is repeated here. `ipc.rs`'s `the_acl_grants_the_main_window_the_core_commands_its_title_bar_calls` asks the shipped RuntimeAuthority for all seven commands the bar depends on, so the three that arrive through `core:default` (`is_maximized`, `internal_toggle_maximize`, `plugin:event|listen`) are held as firmly as the four named below. Nothing that SETS a window property is granted - no set-decorations, no set-always-on-top, no set-position, no set-size - because the bar reads the window's state and drives the three controls a window has, and nothing more.
